Hey world, my name is Manish. I am a researcher, and I am starting a deep dive into CS336, where I want to implement each component of an LLM and understand it inside out.
This is my diary of the notes I take while I learn this and attempt the assignments. Let’s have fun.

title: Starting CS336
text:
A first code cell
This is just a test to check if the plots render correctly on this blog.


Code
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.patches import FancyBboxPatch

INK, BLOCK, NORM, EDGE = "#1f2937", "#dbeafe", "#f3f4f6", "#1e40af"

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 7.5))
ax.set_xlim(0, 10)
ax.set_ylim(0.3, 13)
ax.axis("off")


def box(y, label, fc, w=6, h=0.9):
    ax.add_patch(FancyBboxPatch((5 - w / 2, y - h / 2), w, h,
                 boxstyle="round,pad=0.05,rounding_size=0.15", fc=fc, ec=EDGE, lw=1.2))
    ax.text(5, y, label, ha="center", va="center", fontsize=9, color=INK)


def arrow(x0, y0, x1, y1):
    ax.annotate("", xy=(x1, y1), xytext=(x0, y0),
                arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-|>", color=INK, lw=1.2))


def residual(ya, yb):
    ax.plot([2.0, 1.0, 1.0], [ya, ya, yb], color=INK, lw=1.2)
    arrow(1.0, yb, 2.0, yb)


layers = [
    (1.0, "Input tokens", "white"),
    (2.6, "Token embedding + positional encoding", NORM),
    (4.2, "Multi-head self-attention", BLOCK),
    (5.6, "Add & Norm", NORM),
    (7.0, "Feed-forward network", BLOCK),
    (8.4, "Add & Norm", NORM),
    (9.8, "Linear + softmax", BLOCK),
    (11.2, "Next-token probabilities", "white"),
]
for y, label, fc in layers:
    box(y, label, fc)
for (y0, _, _), (y1, _, _) in zip(layers, layers[1:]):
    arrow(5, y0 + 0.45, 5, y1 - 0.45)

residual(2.6, 5.6)
residual(5.6, 8.4)

ax.add_patch(plt.Rectangle((0.3, 3.5), 9.4, 5.45, fill=False, ls="--", ec="#6b7280", lw=1))
ax.text(9.5, 3.7, "× N", ha="right", va="bottom", fontsize=10, color="#6b7280")

plt.show()
